historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (+6.2%) diverges by far more than 30% from EPS (-18.0% 5-year, -17.8% 3-year). FY2026 EPS of $1.68 carries a $141.3M non-deductible goodwill impairment and restructuring; FY2021-FY2023 revenue was inflated by the used-car price spike. Neither CAGR is a usable forward anchor, so growth is built from units, price and guidance instead.
historical_growth.notes: FY2026 (Feb-2026) against FY2023 and FY2021. Owner-FCF CAGRs are not computable: the owner-FCF series (OCF + net non-recourse note issuance - capex - SBC) is FY2024 380.5, FY2025 274.6, FY2026 -148.3, ending negative. The series was rebuilt for three years only; earlier years need the non-recourse note flows from older filings not on hand. Reported OCF-less-capex FCF is dominated by CAF loan-book movements and is not comparable.

scenario_narratives.base: The H1 FY2027 rebound (comparable units +13% in Q2 after -9% in Q3 FY2026) proves that sharper pricing buys volume, at a cost of roughly $150-200 of used gross profit per unit. Unit growth settles at 2-3% a year on four store openings and a slow share recovery from 3.6% of the 0-10 year-old market. The $200M SG&A programme lands but about half is reinvested in price and marketing. CAF penetration drifts from ~42% toward the mid-40s with Tier 2 losses in line with pricing, so CAF income grows roughly with the book. Owner EBIT settles near 3.45% of revenue, above FY2025 and far below the pre-2020 level.
scenario_narratives.bull: Shift into GEAR works: lower prices funded by reconditioning and logistics savings restore share gains against Carvana and franchised dealers, with mid-single-digit unit growth for several years. SG&A per unit falls as volume leverages a fixed store and technology base. CAF reaches the 50% penetration goal with full-spectrum underwriting performing to model (each point worth $10-12M of lifetime pre-tax income per origination year), and off-balance-sheet loan sales recycle capital. Owner EBIT reaches ~4.2% of revenue, still below FY2019.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY2027 volume gain turns out to be bought, not earned: Carvana and dealer groups match price, units stall, and used gross profit per unit does not recover. The Tier 2 expansion (target raised to ~30% of Tier 2 volume, allowance already 3.07% of loans) meets a weaker consumer, and provisions rise as with the 2022-2023 vintages, cutting CAF income just as ABS spreads widen. A new outside CEO resets strategy again. Owner EBIT stays near 2.2% of revenue, roughly the FY2026 level before restructuring.

valuation_philosophy.summary: CarMax is valued as one operating business with its finance arm inside it. CAF income is counted after its own funding cost and credit losses, and the non-recourse securitization debt that funds the loans is left out of net debt; only the ~$1.9B of recourse debt and finance-lease obligations is deducted. Margins are built from components on a revenue base that grows at a low-single-digit rate after the FY2027 rebound, growth is charged for the inventory and loan-book equity it consumes, and the terminal multiple is capped at 14x owner FCF because this is a cyclical, thin-margin retailer.
key_risks_to_valuation: CAF income (~$560M pre-tax) exceeds half of operating profit; a credit cycle in the Tier 2 expansion or a closed ABS market hits the margin path directly, and the model discounts that levered stream at a blended WACC rather than a pure cost of equity
Value is highly sensitive to the mature margin: each 0.5pp of EBITDA margin is roughly $190M of pre-tax profit against an equity value of about $7B
Working-capital intensity: at -14% of incremental revenue, faster growth lowers near-term free cash flow; a lower inventory requirement would raise value in every scenario
FY2027 guidance year rests on one strong half; Q3 and Q4 FY2027 lap easy comparisons and a $50M pension settlement charge (non-recurring, excluded from the flows) will depress reported earnings

FY0 owner FCF is negative and the three-year owner-FCF history averages ~$170M a year, well below the $450-900M the base case projects from FY2028; the valuation depends on capex staying near $400-450M and margins recovering

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 31.95-65.28
data_sources.financials: CarMax 10-K FY2026 (fiscal year ended 2026-02-28) and 10-Q Q2 FY2027 (2026-08-31) text in research/KMX/Extracted; KMX_Metrics.csv and kpis for history

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: Q2 FY2027 10-Q weighted average common shares and dilutive potential common shares, 142.450M (141.934M issued and outstanding at 2026-08-31 plus ~0.5M dilutive). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; buybacks were paused in H1 FY2027 ($2.6M) and are the mechanism that would fund the flat count once resumed.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement, share-based compensation expense $99.018M (KMX_Annual_FY2026.txt:3059). Includes cash-settled RSUs ($30.4M), which are liability awards paid in cash; no separate equity-award withholding-tax line is disclosed in financing activities, so nothing is added on top. FY2026 was depressed by the share-price fall (FY2025: $134.7M, 0.51% of revenue; H1 FY2027: $74.3M, 0.47%), so the forward path uses 0.45%, not the FY2026 0.38%.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free 5.15% (US 10-year, Yahoo ^TNX at the valuation date), ERP 4.5%, beta ~1.2 gives cost of equity ~10.5%; corporate (recourse) debt ~$1.9B at ~6.5% pre-tax, ~4.9% after tax; weights ~80/20 on market values give 9.4%, rounded up to 9.5%. Rounded up deliberately: CAF income inside the flows is an equity-like, post-funding-cost stream on a book levered ~19x by non-recourse notes, so the blended rate should sit nearer the cost of equity than a plain retailer's WACC. Same WACC in all three scenarios; cyclical and credit risk are carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Split by lease type, each charged once. Operating leases (liability $496.0M) are treatment B: US GAAP straight-line rent is already inside SG&A and therefore inside the EBITDA margin, so lease_cost_pct_path is 0 and the liability is excluded from net debt. Finance leases ($199.1M) and sale-leaseback financing obligations ($482.5M) are treatment A: their interest sits below EBIT and their depreciation in D&A, so both liabilities are in total_debt.
inputs.caf_treatment: CarMax Auto Finance is consolidated into the owner-FCF flows, not valued as a separate lender. CAF income ($562.7M FY2026) is reported after interest on the non-recourse notes ($769.2M), after the loan-loss provision ($391.2M) and after direct CAF costs, so it enters the EBITDA margin as a post-funding-cost stream. Consistently, the $15,721.3M of non-recourse notes payable is treated as segment funding secured on $16,198.7M of auto loans and is EXCLUDED from net debt, as is the $604.9M of restricted cash held in the securitization trusts. Subtracting the notes after including CAF income would deduct the funding twice. The equity slice CarMax must fund as the loan book grows (overcollateralization plus allowance, roughly 5% of receivables) is charged through the negative wc_capture_pct alongside inventory.
inputs.net_debt_build: Recourse debt only, 2026-08-31 10-Q: current portion of long-term debt $17.7M + long-term debt $1,663.3M (term loans $998.7M, 4.27% senior notes $200.0M, financing obligations $482.5M; revolver undrawn) + finance lease liabilities $199.1M = $1,880.1M; less unrestricted cash $170.5M = $1,709.6M. XBRL/CSV total_debt of ~$17.4B includes the non-recourse notes and must not be used.
inputs.fcf_definition: The CSV free_cash_flow (OCF less capex, $1,242.9M FY2026) is not a usable FCF for this company: auto-loan originations and collections run through operating activities while their non-recourse funding runs through financing. reported_fcf here is OCF + net issuance of non-recourse notes - capex: FY2026 1,783.8 - 1,292.1 - 541.0 = -49.3; FY2025 624.4 + 252.8 - 467.9 = 409.3; FY2024 458.6 + 506.9 - 465.3 = 500.2. Owner FCF (less SBC): FY2024 380.5, FY2025 274.6, FY2026 -148.3. FY2026 is negative because of a $202M inventory build, peak capex ($541M versus ~$400M guided for FY2027) and restructuring; it is not a run-rate, and the component build does not start from it.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the cyclical/lease adaptations. Routing: CarMax is an operating retailer (used-vehicle retail and wholesale auctions) with a captive lender. A separate sum-of-parts was considered and rejected: CAF originates only at CarMax stores, CAF income carries no allocation of store or corporate cost, and excluding it leaves the retail segment at roughly break-even, so a split would value two parts that cannot exist apart on an arbitrary cost allocation. Instead CAF is consolidated as a post-funding-cost income stream with its non-recourse debt treated as operating funding (see caf_treatment). FY0 margin anchors (FY2026, pre-SBC EBITDA): gross profit 2,806.6 + CAF income 562.7 - SG&A 2,453.4 - income-statement D&A 273.8 - other expense 7.1 = EBIT before interest and goodwill impairment of 635.1; plus total D&A 346.0 (cash flow statement, including ~72 carried in cost of sales) plus SBC 99.0 = 1,080.1, 4.17% of revenue (FY2025 4.62%; H1 FY2027 4.97% in the seasonally stronger half). The $141.3M Edmunds goodwill impairment is non-cash and excluded. Buybacks: $642.8M in FY2026, paused in H1 FY2027 while leverage was above target, $1.31B authorization remaining; the flat share count is a funded convention historically. Price is a regular-session close. A fall strategic update was scheduled for 2026-11-03; its content is not in the filings on hand and is not reflected.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027: H1 revenue +12.4% (Q2 comparable units +13.0%, ASP +6%), lapping a weak H2 FY2026; 11% for the year assumes H2 slows a little. Then unit growth of 2-3% (four stores a year on 258, modest share gain from 3.6%) plus 1-2% price.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA margin: FY2026 4.17%, FY2025 4.62%, H1 FY2027 4.97%. FY2027 4.6% reflects H1 actuals and guided used GPU down less than $200/unit. FY2028 steps up on the full $200M SG&A exit-rate savings (about half reinvested or offset) and the +$35/unit EPP redesign. Mature 5.2% equals owner EBIT of ~3.45% of revenue, above FY2025's 2.9% and well below the 6%+ of FY2019, because ASPs rose ~35% while gross profit per unit stayed near $2,200-2,300.
base.tax_rationale: Effective rate 25.2-25.3% in FY2024-FY2025; FY2026 35.5% is the non-deductible impairment. Cash taxes paid have run at or below the provision; 25% held flat.
base.wc_rationale: Negative: growth consumes cash. Inventory is ~16% of revenue against payables of ~4%, plus the ~5% equity slice of a CAF book that is ~60% of revenue. Inventory at 2026-08-31 was ~$500M above a year earlier on a ~$3B revenue run-rate increase, i.e. roughly 16%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% default: more than half of operating profit is CAF income from a ~19x-levered loan book that is moving down the credit spectrum, the strategy is new and led by a CEO from outside the industry, and FY2026 showed how fast units and margins fall together. Base 50%: it is anchored on two reported quarters of recovery and explicit FY2027 guidance for margin, SG&A and capex. Bull cut to 25% from 35%: it needs sustained share gains, SG&A leverage and clean Tier 2 credit performance at the same time.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
